speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your symptoms better, could you tell me if the double vision and weakness fluctuate throughout the day or worsen with repeated use of those muscles?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any difficulty swallowing, speaking, or breathing, especially towards the end of the day? I would also like to examine your eye movements to check for ptosis or limited range of motion.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any difficulty swallowing, speaking, or breathing, especially towards the end of the day? I would also like to examine your eye movements to check for ptosis or limited range of motion.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: I will now examine your eyes to check for drooping eyelids or limited eye movement. Please follow my finger with your eyes without moving your head.

speaker: Patient
text: The weakness is clearly worse with exertion and better after rest. I have not noticed muscle wasting or weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your symptoms of fluctuating weakness and diplopia, I need to rule out neuromuscular junction disorders. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine receptor antibody test. REQUEST TEST: Repetitive nerve stimulation.
